entities.summary: Jakub Świnka was a Polish Catholic priest, the Archbishop of Gniezno and a notable politician and statesman, supporter of the idea of unification of all Polish lands under the rule of Władysław I the Elbow-high. His coat of arms was Świnka.

entities.summary:
Jakub Świnka was a Polish Catholic priest and statesman who played a pivotal role in the unification of Polish lands under the rule of Władysław I the Elbow-high. Born in 1300, Świnka served as the Archbishop of Gniezno, a position he held from 1310 until his death in 1313.



As a key figure in Polish politics, Świnka supported the idea of unification, which had significant consequences for the region. His influence extended beyond Poland, with the Polish-Lithuanian union that he helped establish having far-reaching implications for Eastern European history.



Despite his significant contributions, Świnka's legacy is often overshadowed by that of other historical figures. Nevertheless, his role in shaping the course of Polish history remains an important aspect of the region's rich cultural heritage.



This enigmatic figure's life and legacy continue to fascinate historians and scholars, who seek to understand the complex web of events and relationships that shaped his time.
